findings.what: The four constant-acceleration equations the brief promises (v = u + at, s = ½(u + v)t, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as) are on no screen: they live only in the explain text, which a steps lesson never shows, so name each one where its picture already stands (slope on 1, rectangle plus triangle on 3, average speed on 4) and add one puzzle that needs v² = u² + 2as.

The why of impulse is skipped: the screen says 1000 N s 'gives' 1000 kg m/s but never shows force × time = mass × acceleration × time = mass × change in speed, nor that a newton is a kg m/s², so move the moment sentence into the beam's label to make room for those two lines.

The 500 kg m/s that A loses and B gains and the 0.25 m/s shared speed appear with no working, at the one place where the force pair and impulse combine into conservation, so show 1000 N × 0.5 s = 500 N s on each and 1000 ÷ 4000 = 0.25 m/s.

The equal and opposite 1000 N arrows show only during the 0.5 s press (two frames of the film), and the settled picture and the read-through still have no forces at all, so the screen's main sentence has nothing to point at once it settles: keep the pair drawn after the press, labelled 'while the buffers pressed, 0.5 s', or give the step a still at mid-press.

Each slope is a filled amber triangle the same size as the distance triangle under the line, so a shaded triangle means slope above the line and distance below it, the very mix-up puzzle 2 tests; draw the slope as outlined rise and run legs and keep fill for the area alone.
'Net force = mass × acceleration' arrives as a bare rule; one short sentence (more net force gives more acceleration, more mass gives less) would let him reason with it rather than recall it.
'Stops 10 s and 2.5 m later' gives no working, but there are 79 words, so add 0.5 ÷ 0.05 = 10 s and ½ × 10 × 0.5 = 2.5 m, an easy recall of slope and area.
The triangle is worked as ½ × 0.25 × 2², a formula nobody has named yet; either say it is ½ × a × t², the ut + ½at² equation, or write ½ × 2 × 0.5 as base × height.
Only speed and distance are used: velocity and displacement, which the brief promises and momentum's direction depends on, are never named, so one sentence on screen 1 or 9 would build on Vectors.
Nothing ties the slope and the area to the derivative and integral he already knows, which the brief lists as this lesson's recall; one sentence would make it a review rather than a new idea.
The caption about the force graph following the slope shows from screen 1 and on puzzles with no force graph, before net force is met on screen 5; show it from screen 7 on.
A picked answer is filled in ink, exactly like the Check button below it, so the choice and the action look the same; a tick or a heavier outline would tell them apart.
'The drive gives 600 N, as friction takes 100 N' can read as 'while'; 'The drive gives 600 N: 500 N net plus the 100 N friction takes' is plainer.
